title: Task 6 mage/prebuff pinned-source checkpoint
question: Which source stages and exceptions must a bounded mage/prebuff pilot preserve before effective-script comparison?

environment.description: Read-only HTTPS source inspection in memory; authored metadata and offline tests only.

versions.fingerprint: Per-file raw-byte SHA-256 recorded below; not an installed-stack fingerprint.

method.summary: Fetch exact pinned files as raw bytes into memory, compute SHA-256, number UTF-8 lines by LF boundaries, inspect selected ranges and trace caller-to-template references; retain only authored facts/digests/links.
constraints: No installed game, save, lab, or effective resource accessed.
No upstream source, generated script, rule table, or decompile committed.
No SSL compiler, WeiDU, Lua, or game process executed.
Offline document checks do not prove the source claims or runtime semantics.

observations: Component 6030 invokes the mage entry after the AI-initialization prerequisite; shared generation selects templates and spell inputs, then emits and inserts a script.
The standard mage combat include list is nested inside a larger main script; encounter-specific code is not confined to separate encounter directories.
Generic short and long prebuff templates explicitly remove a spell, but special PRECAST/resource/innate branches differ.
The CorePlusPrep source references the general difficulty variable; some neighboring prep triggers reference the prep-specific variable. Names alone are not a semantic contract.
counterevidence: Special no-decrement and PRECAST paths refute a universal rule that every prebuff removes a memorized spell.
The shared core includes Kruin-specific logic, so a common template is not proof of generic actor eligibility.
No effective BCS, complete macro expansion, or runtime comparison was collected; actual output may differ with inputs, libraries, and later patches.

claims.statement: The inspected source separates component invocation, creature/spell selection, SSL generation and BCS publication/insertion.
limitations: Caller/template source trace only; not proof of actual compilation, final install order, creature slot, or external-control closure.

claims.statement: The standard combat include sequence is downstream of setup, defensive and movement-related main-script stages.
limitations: Authored include order only; macro pruning, response weights, Continue behavior and final BCS remain unverified.

claims.statement: Generic SpellPrecast and SpellPrecastLong explicitly pair force-spell actions with RemoveSpell and Continue; other inspected paths do not use that accounting.
limitations: No assertion that queued actions completed or expenditure occurred; special generated spell payloads and one-shot reset/control closure remain unresolved.

claims.statement: The source contains target/protection macro calls and named encounter gates within shared mage/prebuff files.
limitations: Called target/protection macro bodies are not expanded here; no encounter ownership claim.

claims.statement: The prep source distinguishes duration families, sight/proximity conditions, settings and special branches, with a general-versus-prep difficulty-variable distinction.
limitations: Duration comments are categorization intent, not verified SPL duration; exact effective predicate expansion and runtime fairness remain open.
